 Barely a peep from Tkachuk Bros. as Edmonton Oilers humble Florida Panthers
 Author of the article: By Robert Tychkowski Published Nov 17, 2026 Last updated 8 hours ago 4 minute read Join the conversation Florida Panthers Seth Jones defends against Edmonton Oilers Connor McDavid during the third period at Amerant Bank Arena on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026 in Sunrise, Fla. The Oilers defeated the Panthers 5-2. Photo by Bruce Bennett / Getty Images Article content The Edmonton Oilers are running so hot right now that they can make a game with the Florida Panthers seem routine.

Activate your Online Access Now Article content This is a bitter rivalry that stops traffic around the NHL, but the Oilers turned Tuesday’s hotly anticipated showdown into a foregone conclusion, running the Panthers out of their rink almost from the start of a 5-2 Edmonton victory.
 Article content We apologize, but this video has failed to load. Try refreshing your browser, or
 tap here to see other videos from our team . Back to video 
 Article content The Panthers made it look closer than it was with a couple of goals in garbage time, but when it mattered the Oilers beat the Panthers in pretty much every way you can beat a hockey team. Their offence pumped them for five goals. The defence held them to 23 shots. They were heavier. Their power play scored two goals. Their penalty kill was perfect. Their goaltending was way better. And their coach made a subtle line shuffle that seemed to spark the 60-minute onslaught.

Article content And if anyone was expecting the reunited Tkachuk brothers were going to have a major impact — perhaps finding a way to bully and antagonize the Oilers off their game — it didn’t happen. Matthew and Brady were pretty much invisible, going minus two on Edmonton’s first two even-strength goals.

 Article content “I liked us, to tell you the truth,” said head coach Mike Babcock. “I thought we were all right. Our power play was good, obviously, but we controlled the game.”
 Article content The Panthers will always have their rings from two Stanley Cup Final wins over Edmonton, but in the here and now this doesn’t even look like a contest.
 Article content This runs Edmonton’s streak to six wins in a row, 10-0-1 on the road and 17-3-3 on the season.
 Article content It’s not like the Panthers are a pushover, they were 10-5-1 in the 16 games leading up to this, but they looked overwhelmed when Edmonton applied the pressure.
 Article content Babcock changed up his lines, putting Leon Draisaitl between Kasperi Kapanen and Vasily Podkolzin and it paid immediate dividends. Kapanen scored in the first period and Podkolzin in the second.
 Article content “We knew that with Nuge (Ryan Nugent-Hopkins) out we probably weren’t deep enough to go the way we’ve been going,” said Babcock, who didn’t want to let the Panthers know this was coming any sooner than he had to.
 Article content Advertisement 2 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content “We knew this morning what we were doing but we kind of waited till game time to make the decision. We could have done this a number of times but I liked the way we’ve been going.”

 Article content Podkolzin finished with two goals and an assist, Kapanen and Draisaitl had a goal and two assists each.
 Article content “We played together last year and in the playoffs. We know each other pretty well,” said Podkolzin, who still pinches himself when he thinks about who he’s been playing with this season.
 Article content “I’m the luckiest guy in the NHL right now to have teammates like that. It’s difficult sometimes, but it’s unreal.”
 Article content Connor McDavid extended his scoring streak to 23 games with a goal and an assist on the power play. It’s the fourth-longest run from the start of a season in NHL history. Wayne Gretzky and Mats Sundin are tied for second at 30 games and Gretzky, of course, made it 51 games in 1983-84.
 Article content McDavid also passed Wayne Gretzky for most power play points as an Oiler (441), but Gretzky put his 439 points up in 696 games while McDavid needed 817 games to pass him.
 Article content Devon Levi, with his parents in the crowed to watch the game, is now 10-1 as an Oilers goalie, with a shutout streak that lasted 148 minutes and 46 seconds until Matthew Tkachuk got a couple past him when the game was already in the books, making it 4-1 at 13:51 and 4-2 at 16:50. Before that, Levi’s last goal against was 5:05 into the second period against the New York Rangers two starts ago.

 Article content The Oilers are 3-0 at the halfway mark of their six-game road trip, having outscored the opposition 13-4. They’ve scored three or more goals in 20 of 23 games this year and they’ve held their opponents to two or fewer goals in nine of the last 11 games.
 Article content Jake (The Forgotten Man) Walman was a healthy scratch again for the sixth game in a row and ninth time in the last 11 games while Nugent-Hopkins missed his second game in a row but the Oilers are being tight-lipped about the reason.
